title: ResortFlow Normalized Tool Error Envelope
description: Permanent home: docs/contracts/schemas/tool-error.schema.json. Every MCP tool call that fails normalizes to this shape, regardless of which of the three vendor envelope shapes produced it (dining's {error:{code,detail,retryable}}, ticketing's {fault:{type,message,detail,retry_after_seconds}}, or the flat/legacy/status-only shapes used by amenities, pms and casino). See specs/001-contracts-foundation/data-model.md for the classification table this schema's error_class enum is derived from. Amended by feature 003-mcp-tool-layer (ADR-015, docs/adr/015-tool-error-envelope-amendment.md) to add completed_sub_calls and effect_status — both optional and additive; no field, requirement, or enum value present before this amendment changed shape or meaning.

error_class.description: The field an agent branches on. Total and deterministic per FR-014.

detail.description: Human-readable, redacted before persistence. Never contains PII.

vendor_code.description: The vendor's own code, when the vendor publishes one (dining, ticketing). Null for status-only vendors (amenities, pms, casino).

retry_after_seconds.description: Present only when error_class is RETRYABLE and the vendor supplied a wait interval.

idempotency_key.description: The key the failing call was made with, so a retry or ledger reconciliation can be joined to this failure.

trace_id.description: Correlates this failure to its telemetry span. See observability/attributes.py.

completed_sub_calls.description: Populated only when this failure came from a composite tool (one call composing several vendor operations, per mcp-tool-contract.md's tool-ergonomics guidance) and at least one of its sub-calls had already completed when a later one failed. Absent or null otherwise. See specs/003-mcp-tool-layer/data-model.md.

effect_status.description: Present and set to "unresolved" only when this failure's error_class does not affirmatively rule out the mutating call's vendor-side effect having taken place (an indeterminate commit outcome, or a schema-invalid response to a mutating call). error_class and effect_status are orthogonal — see specs/003-mcp-tool-layer/spec.md's clarification on this point. Absent or null for every other failure, including all read-only-tool failures.
